Definition: from G804; security (literally or figuratively):--certainty, safety.
BiblicalUsage: This word means safety and certainty, and Luke uses it for the very purpose of his Gospel, that Theophilus might know the certainty of the things he had been taught. The prison keepers claimed the apostles were shut up safely, and Paul warns that the world will cry peace and safety just before sudden destruction comes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe real safety is not a locked door or a comforting slogan, it is knowing the truth for certain. The keepers' safety was an empty cell and the world's safety is a trap, but Luke's certainty still stands.
